gaps: Residency rules cannot be tied to specific requirements: at least 30 credits (normally the final 30) must be completed at UMGC, half the credits within the major must be completed at UMGC, and at least 15 upper-level credits (300–499) must be completed at UMGC. The capture does not say which specific courses must be taken at UMGC.

The capture does not list course codes or titles for the Arts and Humanities, Behavioral and Social Sciences, and science blocks. It gives only the eligible disciplines, and states that 'Science courses in other disciplines may also apply' without saying which ones.
The capture does not define 'a mathematics course approved by the department'.

Sequencing and grade conditions apply but are not credit requirements: a minimum grade of C in major courses and a 2.0 overall GPA; WRTG 112 with C- or better within the first 24 credits; Mathematics within the first 24 credits; the professional exploration course within the first 6 credits.

At least half the major credits must be earned through graded coursework. Pass/fail credit (maximum 18) applies to electives only. General education courses may not double-count toward major or elective requirements.
No related requirements are listed for the BA in History. The general 0–21 related-credit range is not specified for this major.
CAPL 398A Career Planning Management (1) appears in the recommended sequence as an elective only. It is not a stated required course.

transferMaxCredits.basis: 120 degree credits minus the 90-credit transfer ceiling. The school also requires 15 upper-level credits at the school; 21 upper-level credits in this program (named courses and upper-level-only choices) have no outside option, so the plan always meets it.

alternativeMaxCredits.basis: UMGC counts ACE- and NCCRS-evaluated noncollegiate courses as an external source of credit, limited by the combined maximum from all external sources (45 associate, 90 bachelor’s). No separate ceiling for ACE/NCCRS credit is published.

quotes.text: You must complete a minimum of 120 credits.
At least 15 credits of upper-level coursework (i.e., earned in courses numbered 300 to 499) must be completed at UMGC.

upperLevelMinimum.basis: UMGC’s bachelor’s degree requirements set no degree-wide upper-level minimum. Their only upper-level rule is 15 upper-level credits (courses numbered 300 to 499) completed at UMGC. This plan’s named upper-level courses with no outside option total 6 of 15 credits, so meeting the rule depends on the student’s choices.
